headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0119 — Your Slack connection changed while SMTO was using it

html:
SMTO-SKL-0119 — Your Slack connection changed while SMTO was using it

GUID: 06325c31-f012-5eb0-ba82-b4aa0b1ca623
Slug: slack-workspace-changed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • The saved Slack connection or Slack app entry was edited, reconnected or disconnected partway through this request. SMTO stopped rather than carry on with changed details. Steps before the change may already have happened in Slack.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the request was posting or changing something in Slack, open Slack first and check whether it already happened. Steps finished before the change stay done, and repeating them could post twice.
  2. Open Parameter Store from the More options menu and check the Slack workspace and Slack OAuth App entries are the ones you expect. Avoid editing them while a Task uses Slack. SMTO stops whenever these entries are edited, reconnected or disconnected during a request.
  3. If you were connecting Slack, ask SMTO to connect again and finish Slack's page without running other Slack Tasks meanwhile. SMTO saves a sign-in only if the entry hasn't changed since the sign-in link was created.
  4. Then, only for anything that didn't already happen, ask again in a new message, typing @ and picking the Slack workspace entry. Naming the workspace makes SMTO use its current details.

What success looks like

  • The new request finishes in the workspace you named without this message, and nothing appears twice in Slack.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit or disconnect a Slack connection while a Task that uses it is still running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Slack workspace or Slack OAuth App record changed (created_at/updated_at revision or identity fields) between binding and use, during an accepted @ reference check, consent completion, token refresh, token save, disconnect or a Slack request, so SMTO refused to continue.

What this means

  • Accepted bindings, token save/disconnect fences or live app/profile checks detect changed revisions or identity. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Accepted bindings, token save/disconnect fences or live app/profile checks detect changed revisions or identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact profile revisions and inspect prior request receipts.

How to fix it

  • Reload the slack_workspace and slack_oauth_app records and confirm the intended identity (workspace_id, principal_type, user_id, oauth_app_ref, revisions). Check Slack for effects of any write already dispatched in the operation before repeating it, then reconnect with slack.connect if the identity changed, or start a fresh request bound to the current record; never substitute another workspace or principal.
  • Reload the exact workspace and app profiles, inspect any possible effects, and reconnect if the selected identity changed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Further work uses a deliberately selected current identity after prior effects are reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
